papers.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Control for Smooth and Accurate Circular Trajectory Tracking in Mobile Robots
papers.summary: This paper investigates reinforcement learning-based control for smooth and accurate trajectory tracking of a nonholonomic mobile robot. Three reinforcement learning algorithms, Deep Q-Network (DQN), Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), are implemented and evaluated, with conventional PID and Sliding Mode Control (SMC) controllers included as comparative baselines. The robot is modeled using unicycle kinematics, and the tracking task is formulated through body-frame longitudinal, lateral, and heading errors. papers.title: Active Microrobotic Sampling for Embodied Biological Digital Twins at the Limit STARLI Research Works Institute XXVIII Extension 06 English Description This high-density research monograph turns the biological digital twin from a passive recipient of measurements into an embodied experimental partner. Competing twins use uncertainty, expected information gain, physical reachability, safety, authorization, assay burden and traceability to propose the next microrobotic sampling location, time and analyte. The twin remains a versioned scientific belief rather than a replica of a patient, tissue or living system. Central Contribution The Active Sampling Evidence Charter binds twin ancestry, candidate and rejected actions, expected information gain, safety calculations, authorization state, robot trajectory, quantum and classical raw measurements, structured residuals, model forks, resets, abstentions and human overrides into one replayable evidence object. A quantum measurement qualifies only when it reduces biological sampling burden or improves mechanism discrimination against the best classical readout. papers.title: Nonequilibrium energetics of sensing and actuation by a smart active particle
papers.summary: Abstract Smart active agents must allocate finite energetic resources across distinct functions, yet the underlying thermodynamic trade-offs remain poorly understood. Here, we introduce a minimal model of a self-steering particle with an internal polarity-cue sensor coupled to an external environmental field, decomposing its steady-state entropy production rate into locomotion, actuation, and sensing costs. papers.title: Adversarial Multi-Agent RL for Grant-Free NORA Control in Ultra Dense Network under Asymmetric Uncertainty
papers.summary: Grant-free nonorthogonal random access (NORA) enables scalable access in hyper-dense IoT networks by combining ALOHA-type transmission with nonorthogonal multiple access, eliminating base station handshaking and reducing signaling overhead. However, its performance decreases severely under heavy collisions and interference when the user density is high. papers.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning for Energy Management of EV-Integrated Renewable Microgrids in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Methodology Proposal
papers.summary: Energy management in solar-based microgrids that also serve electric vehicles (EVs) in sub-Saharan Africa must cope with scarce measurement data, unreliable grid supply, volatile demand and tight battery and generator limits. Reinforcement learning (RL) can adapt to this uncertainty, but unconstrained RL policies give no assurance that operating limits are respected, and most published methods are validated on data-rich systems outside the region. papers.title: A wire-driven robotic shark with a non-uniform stiffness distribution fish tail
papers.summary: Inspired by the muscle-driven mechanisms of natural fish, wire-driven robotic fish have emerged as a prominent research focus. This paper presents a wire-driven robotic shark (WRS) featuring a flexible tail with non-uniform stiffness distribution. papers.summary: DNA nanomachines based on gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) are promising platforms for intracellular sensing of microRNAs (miRNAs), which are biomarkers involved in a wide range of diseases.
